course_name_original: FONDAMENTI DI COMUNICAZIONI E INTERNET canale 1
course_name_en: FUNDAMENTALS OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INTERNET channel 1
prerequisites: Basic programming skills and knowledge of at least one common programming language (e.g. Python)

learning_outcomes.text: Know the concepts underlying digital signal processing, their transmission in current telecommunication networks, access and error control protocols, and network and transport protocols based on the TPC/IP suite.

Be able to understand how continuous and discrete time signal operations work, how a protocol works, what its characterizing functionalities are, and how performance can be evaluated. Be able to perform simple protocol dimensioning at various levels of a telecommunications architecture.
Be able to analyze the benefits and limits of signal operations and dimensioning of protocols or TPC/IP network configurations.
Be able to present the signal processing functionality (correlation, sampling, time or frequency domain analysis) and the operation of a network protocol and discuss its performance.

Beyond the classic learning skills provided by the theoretical study of teaching material, the course delivery methods, particularly the practical exercises (also performed on simulators and with processing software), stimulate students to a procedural and quantitative analysis of network operation and related protocols, facilitating the concrete application of concepts and techniques learned during the course.

Acquire fundamental knowledge related to the organization and operation of telecommunications systems. In particular, know the principles of digital information representation, the characteristics of continuous and discrete-time signals, and the main signal operations. Also acquire basic notions on network architectures, communication protocols, and error control and medium access mechanisms, with particular reference to TCP/IP suite network and transport protocols.

Be able to apply acquired knowledge to analyze and understand the functioning of the main signal operations, both in the time and frequency domains. Be able to interpret the functioning of communication protocols, identify their main functionalities, and evaluate their performance. Also be able to address simple problems of dimensioning and configuration of protocols and components at different levels of a telecommunications architecture.

Develop the ability to critically analyze solutions adopted in telecommunications systems, evaluating the benefits and limits of different signal operations and design choices related to protocols and network configurations based on TCP/IP architectures.

Be able to clearly describe and present the principles of signal processing, such as correlation, sampling, and time and frequency domain analysis, as well as the functioning of network protocols. Also be able to discuss the performance of protocols and communication systems using appropriate technical terminology.

Develop the ability to independently deepen topics related to telecommunications systems and communication networks. Practical exercises and activities, also through the use of simulators and software tools for signal processing and network analysis, will stimulate a procedural and quantitative approach to the study of protocol and network functioning, facilitating the concrete application of acquired knowledge.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to communication networks and the Internet
Evolution of network architectures and telecommunication services
Model and functions of a telecommunication network
Protocol layer and their service models (OSI Reference Model, TCP/IP Architecture)
Fundamentals of digital representations and communications (3 ECTS)
Introduction. Digital representation of information, concept of deterministic signal.
Frequency representation of signals: Fourier transform (continuous and discrete-time signals) and properties
Convolution and correlation between signals. Energy and power spectral density
Signal transit in systems. Properties. Impulse response
Sampling: sampling theorem, Nyquist condition. Analog-to-digital conversion. Quantization and Encoding.
Baseband transmission, multilevel transmission. Noise characterization. Shannon's limit capacity.
Digital modulation: amplitude, frequency, phase. Demodulation. Quadrature Amplitude Modulation.
Definition of signals, operations on signals, correlations
Signal processing in the frequency domain
Multiple Access Protocols (Medium Access Control – MAC)
Network configuration laboratories with Kathara emulation software
Introduction to Linux and virtual machines, installation of Kathara and its configuration
Use of basic Linux terminal commands
Installation of Kathara and testing with basic configuration
Configuration and communication between two hosts
ARP protocol and ARP poisoning laboratory
teaching_methods: In-person lectures with instructor slides and other shared material during the lesson

assessment_methods.method: Homework 2 (network and protocol configuration using Katharà emulation software)
Written exam: 15 multiple-choice questions on theoretical part
Written exam: numerical exercise on practical application of course topics
Oral exam (for exams from March onwards)

assessment_rules: During the course, two intermediate quizzes will be held on Moodle, each contributing up to 2 bonus points, usable only in the January or February exam sessions, for a maximum of 4 bonus points. Two homework assignments contribute 5 points each to the final grade. The written exam consists of 15 multiple-choice questions (15 points) and one numerical exercise (5 points). From March onwards, an oral exam will follow the written test. To pass the exam, a minimum score of 18/30 is required. To achieve 30/30 cum laude, excellent knowledge of all topics, demonstrating logical, coherent, and in-depth connections, is required.
